project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence:
Root cause: net/sf/mpxj/common/InputStreamHelper.java:126, `processZipStream(File dir, InputStream inputStream)` — `File file = new File(dir, entry.getName());` builds the destination path directly from the ZIP entry name (an untrusted value crossing the trust boundary at the point an attacker-supplied/attacker-influenced archive is fed into InputStreamHelper.writeZipStreamToTempDir(InputStream), a public API with no caller-side validation) with no canonical-path containment check. Verified live: reproduced on current code (exit 0) and reproduced-fixed against a representative canonical-path guard inserted at InputStreamHelper.java:126-130 (exit 1), then reverted (git status confirms zero product diff remains).

Every sink fed by that same unsanitized `file`/`parent` must be covered by a complete fix — all reachable from the identical entry.getName() taint source in this one method:
1. InputStreamHelper.java:139 — `new FileOutputStream(file)` — direct file write for a traversal entry name (the path this POV exercises).
2. InputStreamHelper.java:129 → FileHelper.java:95/99 (`FileHelper.mkdirsQuietly(file)`, sink `file.mkdirs()`) — directory-entry case (`entry.isDirectory()`), where a "../"-laden directory entry name causes directory creation outside `dir`.
3. InputStreamHelper.java:133/136 → FileHelper.java:95/99 (`FileHelper.mkdirsQuietly(parent)`, sink `file.mkdirs()`) — the parent-directory creation for a non-directory entry, reachable even for entries whose immediate name is not itself the escape point but whose parent path (via nested "../" segments) is.

All three sinks derive from the single `File file = new File(dir, entry.getName())` at line 126, so a fix at that one construction point (validate/normalize before use) covers all three; a fix applied only at the FileOutputStream call site (sink 1) would leave sinks 2 and 3 exploitable via directory-only entries.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: On unpatched code the test passes (JUnitCore exits 0): InputStreamHelper.writeZipStreamToTempDir() extracts the malicious zip entry "../pov-zipslip-marker-<n>.txt" to a file located in the parent of the returned temp directory (i.e. outside the sandboxed extraction dir), containing the attacker-supplied payload "zip-slip-proof-of-vulnerability". After a correct fix (rejecting/normalizing traversal entries or containing them inside `dir`), the escaped file is never created and the test fails (non-zero exit), either via an explicit IOException from the guard or via the assertion `escapedFile.exists()` failing.
parsed_output.notes:
Targeted alert group's shared root-cause trace: line 126 (`new File(dir, entry.getName())`) feeding into the FileOutputStream write sink at InputStreamHelper.java:139 (the alert's third vulnerability group, single-trace). I chose this as the primary POV because it is the most direct sink from the taint source (no intermediate mkdirsQuietly indirection) and the resulting artifact — a written file with attacker-controlled content outside the sandboxed temp dir — is the clearest, most unambiguous proof of exploitability (arbitrary file write, not merely arbitrary directory creation). The other two alert traces (vulnerability group 1: line 126→129→FileHelper.java:95/99 for directory entries, and line 126→133→136→FileHelper.java:95/99 for parent-directory creation of file entries) share the identical unguarded construction at line 126 and are documented in `evidence`/`regression_hint` so a patch that only special-cases the FileOutputStream call site (and misses the two mkdirsQuietly call sites triggered by directory entries or nested parent paths) will be flagged as incomplete.

Verified end-to-end inside the project container using the provided Docker wrapper: `mvn -B -DskipTests package` to produce target/classes, then javac+java (JUnitCore) against target/classes + the project's bundled junit/hamcrest jars in lib/. Confirmed pov_command exits 0 on the untouched vulnerable source, and exits 1 when a representative canonical-path containment guard is temporarily inserted at InputStreamHelper.java:126-130 (then fully reverted — `git status --porcelain` shows only the untracked `.security-pipeline/` POV directory, zero product diff).
parsed_output.regression_hint:
Invariant: for every ZipEntry extracted in InputStreamHelper.processZipStream, the resolved destination (both the entry's own File and, for non-directory entries, its parent File) must have a canonical path that is equal to, or a strict descendant of, the canonical path of the temp extraction `dir` returned by writeZipStreamToTempDir — i.e. `file.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(dir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator)` (or the file being extracted equals dir itself, though that's not a realistic case). Any entry that fails this check must be rejected (throw, or skip the entry) before any of mkdirsQuietly(file) [line 129], mkdirsQuietly(parent) [line 136], or `new FileOutputStream(file)` [line 139] is invoked — checking only one of the three sinks is insufficient since directory entries and file entries take different branches from the same tainted `file`/`parent` values.

Known bypass variants the fix must also block, not just simple leading "../":
- Nested/mid-path traversal: "sub/../../evil.txt" (parent-directory computation at line 133/136 still escapes even if the literal entry name doesn't start with "../").
- Directory-entry traversal: a ZipEntry with isDirectory()==true and a "../"-laden name, exercised only via the mkdirsQuietly(file) sink at line 129 (never reaches FileOutputStream, so a fix guarding only the file-write branch misses this).
- Absolute path entry names (e.g. "/etc/cron.d/evil" or Windows "C:\\evil"), where `new File(dir, entry.getName())` — because Java's File 2-arg constructor treats an absolute second argument as replacing `dir` entirely on some scenarios/platforms — can resolve completely outside `dir` regardless of ".." segments.
- Backslash-encoded traversal on platforms/JVMs that treat "\\" as a separator, or URL/percent-encoded segments if any decoding occurs upstream of this method.
- Symlink-based escapes: even a name that stays lexically under `dir` could still escape if an intermediate path component is a symlink created by an earlier entry in the same archive — canonicalization (getCanonicalPath, not just getAbsolutePath/normalize) is required to catch this, and ordering-dependent symlink-then-traverse sequences within one archive should be considered.
parsed_output.summary: Created a JUnit4 PoV (ZipSlipPovTest) that feeds a malicious zip through the real public API InputStreamHelper.writeZipStreamToTempDir(InputStream). The zip's only entry is named "../pov-zipslip-marker-<n>.txt". processZipStream() builds `new File(dir, entry.getName())` (InputStreamHelper.java:126) without validating the resolved path stays under `dir`, so the payload is written one directory level above the returned temp extraction directory — a classic Zip Slip / CWE-22 path traversal. The test asserts the escaped file exists outside `dir` with the attacker's content, proving arbitrary-location file write via untrusted archive input.

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root-cause fix in src/main/java/net/sf/mpxj/common/InputStreamHelper.java: added a private static validateZipEntryDestination(File dir, File file) helper that canonicalizes both `dir` and the entry's resolved `file`, and throws IOException if `file`'s canonical path is not equal to, or a strict descendant of, `dir`'s canonical path (using File.separator-based prefix check, which also blocks absolute-path entry names since those still canonicalize outside `dir`). This call was inserted right after `File file = new File(dir, entry.getName())` (originally line 126), before the code branches into the directory-entry mkdirsQuietly(file) path, the parent mkdirsQuietly(parent) path, and the FileOutputStream(file) write path — covering all three sink traces in the alert with one check.

Added a new regression test file src/test/java/net/sf/mpxj/common/InputStreamHelperTest.java covering: (1) a simple "../evil.txt" file-entry traversal, (2) a nested-path traversal where an earlier zip entry creates a real "sub/" directory and a later entry "sub/../../evil.txt" walks back out through it (chosen because a bare single-entry nested-".." pattern incidentally throws FileNotFoundException even on unpatched code, due to how File.mkdirs()/FileOutputStream resolve non-existent intermediate path segments — this two-entry ordering reproduces genuine escape as flagged in the alert's regression_hint about ordering-dependent sequences within one archive), (3) a "../evil-dir/" directory-entry traversal exercising the mkdirsQuietly(file) sink that never reaches FileOutputStream, and (4) a normal non-traversal entry to confirm legitimate extraction still works. Each traversal test independently computes the canonical target the vulnerable code would have written and asserts it does not exist after extraction (or that extraction throws), so the tests are entry-name-driven rather than relying on a hardcoded escape location.

Verified via git stash: with InputStreamHelper.java reverted to the original vulnerable version, all 3 traversal tests fail (3 failures) confirming they genuinely exercise the vulnerability; with the fix restored, all 4 tests pass, and `mvn -B -DskipTests package` builds cleanly.
parsed_output.risk_notes: The fix throws IOException for any zip entry whose resolved path canonicalizes outside the target extraction directory, which changes behavior only for malicious/malformed archives — legitimate archives (entries with relative, non-escaping paths) are unaffected, as shown by the passing testNonTraversalEntryIsExtracted case. writeZipStreamToTempDir() only catches ZipException specifically, so this new IOException propagates to callers exactly as other I/O failures during extraction already did (e.g. a permission-denied mkdir), meaning no new exception-handling contract is introduced. Canonicalization (getCanonicalPath) also incidentally guards against symlink-based escapes noted in the alert's bypass list, since it resolves real paths rather than doing purely lexical normalization. One residual consideration: the check runs per-entry using the entry's own resolved path at processing time, so if a prior entry in the same archive created a symlink that a later entry's path traverses through, canonicalization at the time of the later check still resolves through that real (now-existing) symlink and enforces containment against it — the ordering-dependent regression test added here exercises the closely-related "real intermediate directory from an earlier entry" scenario.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip / path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22) in InputStreamHelper.processZipStream(). The method built extraction destinations directly from untrusted ZipEntry names (`new File(dir, entry.getName())`) with no containment check, letting a malicious archive entry (e.g. "../evil.txt", nested "sub/../../evil.txt", or a "../"-laden directory entry) write files or create directories outside the sandboxed temp extraction directory. Added a single root-cause guard, `validateZipEntryDestination(dir, file)`, called immediately after the `File file = new File(dir, entry.getName())` construction at line 126/127 — before either code path (directory-entry mkdirsQuietly, parent mkdirsQuietly, or FileOutputStream) executes. The guard canonicalizes both the extraction directory and the resolved entry path and throws an IOException unless the entry's canonical path equals or is a strict descendant of the directory's canonical path. Because all three sinks named in the alert (mkdirsQuietly(file) for directory entries, mkdirsQuietly(parent) for file entries, and new FileOutputStream(file)) derive from the same `file` value computed at that one line, this single check blocks all of them, including bypass variants such as mid-path "../" traversal, absolute-path entries, and directory-entry-only traversal.

parsed_output.summary: The patch adds a root-cause containment check (validateZipEntryDestination) in InputStreamHelper.processZipStream, called immediately after `File file = new File(dir, entry.getName())` and before any of the three sinks (mkdirsQuietly(file) for directory entries, mkdirsQuietly(parent) for file entries, and FileOutputStream(file)). It canonicalizes both `dir` and the resolved `file` and throws IOException unless the entry path is `dir` itself or a strict descendant, which blocks the Zip Slip / CWE-22 path traversal (including absolute-path entries and symlink-based escapes, since getCanonicalPath resolves real paths). Independently reran the POV and regression commands via the Docker wrapper against the current worktree state (patch applied): the original PoV (ZipSlipPovTest) now fails with the expected IOException ("Zip entry is outside of the target directory"), confirming the vulnerability no longer reproduces. The new InputStreamHelperTest (4 tests covering simple traversal, nested/mid-path traversal, directory-entry traversal, and a legitimate non-traversal extraction) passes, and `mvn -B -DskipTests package` builds cleanly. The diff is minimal and scoped: only InputStreamHelper.java (22 lines, single new private helper + one call site) was modified in product code, plus a new test file — no unrelated changes, no weakening/removal of legitimate extraction functionality, and the PoV itself was not modified or disabled.
